findings.title: Unvalidated nb_blocks below Argon2 minimum causes heap buffer overflow
findings.evidence: argon2i_32() copies the caller-supplied nb_blocks straight into config.nb_blocks (line 328) without enforcing the documented Monocypher/Argon2 contract 'nb_blocks >= 8 * nb_lanes' (monocypher.h:160, nb_lanes is hard-coded to 1 at line 330). It then sizes the work area from that same untrusted value: work_area = malloc(nb_blocks * 1024) at line 345, and passes both to crypto_argon2 at line 347. In crypto_argon2 (monocypher.c:752-775) the block count is first rounded down: segment_size = nb_blocks/1/4, lane_size = 4*segment_size, so for nb_blocks in 1..3 both segment_size and lane_size become 0. The unconditional 'fill first 2 blocks of each lane' loop (monocypher.c:768-773) writes blocks[0] and blocks[1] (2*1024 bytes) regardless of lane_size. With nb_blocks=1 the allocation is only 1024 bytes, so writing blocks[1] is a 1024-byte heap out-of-bounds write; with nb_blocks=0 malloc(0) is used and both writes go out of bounds. nb_blocks=2..7 additionally makes last_block = blocks + lane_size - 1 underflow / under-allocate relative to the internal block usage. Any application that exposes argon2i_32() parameters (nb_blocks) to an attacker, or accepts them from untrusted configuration/messages, reaches the overflow with a single call such as monocypher.argon2i_32(1, 1, b'pw', b'salt'); memory corruption can be leveraged for further exploitation, and at minimum causes a reliable crash.
